title: Abstract good reduction of a generic torus in a semiabelian family
statement: Let $S$ be normal, integral and locally Noetherian, with generic point $\eta$. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation with semiabelian geometric fibres. Let $V\hookrightarrow G_\eta$ be any closed torus subgroup over $K=\kappa(\eta)$. Then there are a smooth affine faithfully flat commutative group scheme $P\to S$ of finite presentation, fppf locally isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,S}^r$, and an isomorphism $\alpha:P_\eta\simeq V$ of $K$-group schemes. This conclusion specifies an abstract torus model, without specifying a map $P\to G$. For every algebraically closed geometric point $s$, $P_s$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_{m,s}^r$. Rank zero is allowed. The scheme, normality, finite-presentation, group, fibre, torus and topology conventions are [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-sc-group-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] [def-pc-base-change] [def-sc-gm-ga] [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-pc-fppf-site]; affine means that inverse images of affine opens are affine. For a group scheme over $S$, the group diagrams are those of the displayed group-scheme convention with $S$ in place of $\operatorname{Spec}k$: multiplication $G\times_SG\to G$, inverse $G\to G$ and unit $S\to G$.

proof.text: Choose a separable closure $\Omega/K$. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], $V$ splits over a finite separable extension and its geometric character group $M=X^*(V_\Omega)$ has a continuous $\Gamma_K$-action. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-character-reconstruction] over the field $\Omega$ to the split torus: $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r$. Its action has finite image: the intersection of the open stabilizers of a finite basis fixes every element of $M$, so its cosets form a discrete quotient of the compact group $\Gamma_K$, hence are finite. Write $H$ for this finite image and $\rho:\Gamma_K\twoheadrightarrow H$ for the action quotient.

source.place: §3.1.1, Lemma 3.1.1.6; finite image follows from compactness and a finite basis.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-generic-toric-character-local-inertia], every strict local subgroup $J_x$ acts trivially on $M$, so $J_x\subseteq\ker\rho$ for all $x\in S$. The hypotheses there are exactly the given normal integral locally Noetherian base, semiabelian family and closed generic torus. By [lem-dl-a1-normal-scheme-galois-inertia-presentation], $q:\Gamma_K\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(S,\bar\eta)$ has kernel the closed normal subgroup generated by these $J_x$. Since $\ker\rho$ is closed and normal, $\rho$ factors as $\bar\rho q$. This factor is continuous: $q$ is a closed surjection from a compact group to a Hausdorff group, hence a quotient map, and $q^{-1}\bar\rho^{-1}(h)=\rho^{-1}(h)$ is open for every $h\in H$.

source.place: Tag 0BTD, lemma-normal-pione-quotient-inertia (1),(3); local toric input from Lan Proposition 3.3.1.7 in the cited supporting node.

proof.text: Apply [thm-galois-fundamental] to the finite set $H$, with $\pi_1(S,\bar\eta)$ acting by left multiplication through $\bar\rho$. Right translations commute with this action and give a right $H$-action on its finite locally constant sheaf $E$. The regular-action identity makes $E$ an $H$-torsor: the map $E\times H\to E\times E$, $(e,h)\mapsto(e,eh)$, is the image under the equivalence of the bijection $(a,h)\mapsto(a,ah)$. Etale locally $E$ is a nonempty constant sheaf, so local sections trivialize it. Its representing finite etale scheme $Y\to S$ is therefore a surjective right $H$-torsor. The base-change compatibility in the cited theorem identifies its generic monodromy with $\rho$. On $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ define $\mathcal M(U)$ as the sections $a\in\underline M(Y\times_SU)$ satisfying $r_h^*a=h^{-1}a$ for every $h\in H$, where $r_h$ is right translation and $\underline M$ is the constant abelian sheaf. Restrictions and addition are those of $\underline M$. Its sheaf axiom gives unique gluing of these sections and their equivariance equations, so $\mathcal M$ is an abelian sheaf. A local section $y$ of the torsor identifies it with the constant sheaf $M$ by evaluation at $y$; replacing $y$ by $yh$ changes the identification by $h^{-1}$. Thus it is a lattice sheaf of constant rank $r$, and its geometric generic stalk has the original $\Gamma_K$-action on $M$.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group; finite regular action and explicit associated lattice sheaf.

proof.text: Set $P=D_S(\mathcal M)$ using [lem-sfb-relative-torus-character-reconstruction]. It is smooth, affine, faithfully flat, commutative and of finite presentation; the local trivializations of $\mathcal M$ give $P\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ etale locally, hence fppf locally. The base-change identification gives $X^*(P_\eta)=M$ with the action obtained in step 3. Full faithfulness of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] therefore turns the identity of this Galois lattice with $X^*(V)$ into an isomorphism $\alpha:P_\eta\simeq V$. The relative reconstruction theorem also identifies every algebraically closed geometric fibre with $\mathbf G_m^r$. If $r=0$, $M=0$, $H=1$, $\mathcal M=0$ and the represented group is the trivial $S$-group, so all assertions include rank zero.
